clue.text: Sport for minted royals?

blocks.note: surface reading: a game for wealthy members of the royal family, minted being slang for rich
setter's reading: the game shares its name with a well-known brand of mint sweet with a hole in the middle

explanation.surface: A question about which pastime suits a rich royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is the horseback game famously played by British princes, and Polo is also a brand of peppermint, hence minted.
explanation.definitionFit: The horseback stick-and-ball game is strongly associated with royalty and wealth, and also names a mint sweet.

clue.text: A little signage, miniature sign!

indicators.note: only a small portion of the following words is wanted, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a tiny piece of signage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins are one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, so the answer is an astrological sign.

clue.text: Cabaret hit

blocks.note: first meaning: a nightclub with live entertainment
second meaning: to strike with a heavy stick

explanation.walkthrough: Cabaret hit looks like a popular show tune; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot offering entertainment is a club, and to beat someone with a cudgel is to club them.

clue.text: Shooter with gun ultimately breaking law

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word before it is used
breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: a canon is a church law or rule
the last letter of gun

explanation.surface: A gunman ends up on the wrong side of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking here means splitting the law word apart to let the extra letter in, not a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large gun, so it is something that shoots, a fair if loose synonym for shooter.

clue.text: Redesign of trains, so lighter?

definitions.note: a lighter here is a person who lights fires

indicators.note: redesigning something rearranges its parts, so the following letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rebuilding the trains might make them lighter in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Lighter looks like a weight comparison, but it means someone who sets light to things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately sets fires is literally one who lights them, a whimsical noun formed from the verb.

clue.text: Canine, cutie with tail

blocks.note: silly sausage is an affectionate name for a lovable person
to tail someone is to follow them closely, to dog them

explanation.surface: A dog described as a cute thing with a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage sausage is a fond term for a sweet person, and a sausage dog is a dachshund.
explanation.definitionFit: A dachshund, long and low like a sausage, is a breed of dog and so a canine.

clue.text: Come together nicely with casting of vote in parliament

indicators.note: casting things throws them about, so the letters are scattered into a new order
in tells us one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: Things fit neatly when votes are cast in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Casting of vote sounds like voting, but it means the letters are thrown about.
explanation.definitionFit: Dovetail joints interlock perfectly, so to dovetail is to fit or combine together harmoniously.

clue.text: Con isn't working: Muslim official on top of it

indicators.note: something working is in operation, so these letters are put through a change of order
in a down entry, one piece placed on top comes first, ahead of the earlier piece

blocks.note: an aga is a Turkish or Muslim commander or chief
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A scam that fails, with a religious official overseeing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Con looks like a swindle, but it is the opposite of pro, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros and cons are the points for and against, so con is the opposing side.

clue.text: A test of a chamber

blocks.note: taken as written
a trial is a test of something

explanation.surface: An exam room or examination of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an upper chamber of the heart, and the adjective atrial describes that chamber.

clue.text: Historical figure who was exposed as narcissist on journey

indicators.note: on means following after, so the word before it comes second

blocks.note: a go is a trip or outing
a diva is a self-absorbed, vain star

explanation.surface: An egotist is unmasked while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Exposed hints at a scandal but means naked: legend says she rode through Coventry wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Godiva is the eleventh-century noblewoman famed for riding nude through Coventry in protest at taxes.

clue.text: Boycott backed by supporter – some player?

indicators.note: backed by means having something behind it, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: to boycott something is to ban it
a joist is a beam that holds up a floor or ceiling

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, the England cricketer, with a fan behind him, is quite the player.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott suggests the Yorkshire cricketer, while player hints at sport; it is a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjoist is someone who plays the banjo, a specific kind of musical performer, hence some player.

clue.text: A tip containing rubbish, are there splashes of colour in that?

definitions.text: are there splashes of colour in that?

indicators.note: rubbish describes something junked and messed up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all three words taken as written

explanation.surface: A rubbish dump might be strewn with splatters of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip is British for a rubbish dump, which makes rubbish look like part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Action painting is the style of Jackson Pollock and others who dripped and flung paint at the canvas.

clue.text: Once image adjusted and right, one seeing the picture

indicators.note: adjusted letters have been altered in position, so they must be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Once a photo is tweaked and corrected, someone gets the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Seeing the picture sounds like understanding; here the picture is a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is an old word for a film, so someone watching one at the movies is a filmgoer.

clue.text: Sauce, as it's oniony, largely ignored for starters

indicators.note: starters are the first parts, so the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A sauce whose strong onion flavour is mostly overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Oniony is a red herring: the sauce in question is really garlicky.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provencal garlic mayonnaise, a cold sauce served with fish and vegetables.

clue.text: Bird never heard?

indicators.note: heard means we listen to the word rather than read its spelling

blocks.note: not means never in the sense of at no time, and it is said with a silent K in the bird's name

explanation.surface: A bird that has never been heard singing.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a stocky wading sandpiper seen in large flocks on coastal mudflats.

clue.text: What may be sprayed on, fading on the dancefloor?

blocks.note: a spray tan is applied from a mist
going, as in going fast or going away, means fading

explanation.surface: A spray tan wearing off while out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: On the dancefloor describes what someone is doing there: performing an Argentine dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing the tango is a typical activity for dancers, so being on the floor in this sense is a fair cryptic hint.

clue.text: Fish in net's tail thrashing

indicators.note: a tail is the very end, so just the final letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: the last letter of net
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A fish caught in a net flapping its tail about.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrashing looks like an anagram signal but means a heavy defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a common freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Whitewash walls in tower a little bit

indicators.note: walls are the outside of a building, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of tower
an ounce is a tiny amount, as in not an ounce of sense

explanation.surface: Painting the walls of a tower white, only a small patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitewash suggests painting, but in sport it means a total defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash in sport is a crushing win with the losers scoring nothing, so to whitewash is to beat soundly.

clue.text: Still incomplete? Bother!

blocks.note: first meaning: yet to be done, like an item on a list
second meaning: a fuss or commotion

explanation.walkthrough: Bother looks like a mild curse after a task is left unfinished, but it is a noun meaning a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A task still outstanding is one left on the list, while a fuss or kerfuffle is a hyphenated noun with the same letters.

clue.text: Official series featuring old fruit

indicators.note: featuring means including at the front of, so this piece opens the following word

blocks.note: a mandarin is a senior bureaucrat
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a range is a series or line of products

explanation.surface: A civil servant presenting a line of vintage produce.
explanation.walkthrough: Mandarin first suggests the official itself; the fruit only appears with the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin orange is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, related to tangerines and satsumas.

clue.text: Cat discovered and mouse, primarily, in song

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters are stripped away
primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is used

blocks.note: a panther is a big cat
the first letter of mouse

explanation.surface: A cat and a mouse, in a song like a children's nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat is not used as written: it stands for a particular big cat, and discovered then strips that word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing song, such as a national song or a choral piece sung in church.

clue.text: Coming in the year of the Lord, opening

blocks.clueFragment: in the year of the Lord
blocks.note: AD stands for anno Domini, Latin for in the year of the Lord
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Arriving in a holy year, a door opens.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Christian season before Christmas, which is apt as the word names it too.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival, from Latin adventus; the Christian season anticipates Christ's arrival.

clue.text: One doesn't believe it can go wrong potting shrimps, for a start

indicators.note: going wrong means getting mixed up, so these letters are disordered
a start is the beginning, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of shrimps

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that potting shrimps could fail.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is part of the jumbled letters as well as part of the signal, and potting means taking the S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic neither affirms nor denies God's existence, holding it cannot be known, so lacks religious belief.

clue.text: Devious chap, guy seen on and off?

indicators.note: on and off means intermittently, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A shifty man who keeps appearing and disappearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagey means guarded and secretive, unwilling to reveal intentions, close to devious; this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Only purity for rookie?

blocks.note: read as no more than, nothing but
purity is having no vice, so this supplies the sin that is absent

explanation.surface: Is innocence all that a beginner can offer?
explanation.walkthrough: Only purity means nothing wicked at all: NO VICE, run together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a new recruit or beginner, a straightforward synonym for a learner or newcomer.

clue.text: Staff patted themselves on the back?

blocks.note: first meaning: the team working on a ship or film
second meaning: boasted, an old past tense of crow

explanation.surface: Employees congratulated themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Crew is an old past tense of crow, as in the cock crew, and crowing means boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A team of workers is a crew, and archaic crew means crowed, gloated over a success.

clue.text: Villain, name I suspect applied to rogue in the end

indicators.note: as an adjective suspect means dodgy, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order
the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of rogue

explanation.surface: A detective names a suspect, finally pinning it on the scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a nasty or ungenerous person, a playful informal word for a baddie or rotter.

clue.text: Drink where one would be putting meal

blocks.note: on a golf course, putting is done on the green
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A golf clubhouse refreshment between rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Putting is golf, not placing: the putting green.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is unfermented tea from China and Japan, a hot beverage brewed from leaves.
